passages.label: Journal, volume, pages and DOI printed on the article

passages.quote:
Consistent with the findings of Carney et al., our
results showed a significant effect of power posing on
self-reported feelings of power. However, we found no
significant effect of power posing on hormonal levels or
in any of the three behavioral tasks.
passages.label: Opening summary of the study's results (before Method)

passages.quote:
Using a much
larger sample size but similar procedures as Carney et al.
did, we failed to confirm an effect of power posing on
testosterone, cortisol, and financial risk taking. We did
find that power posing affected self-reported feelings of
power; however, this did not yield behavioral effects.
passages.label: Discussion, first paragraph: results restated

passages.quote:
Power Posing: P-Curving the Evidence
Joseph P. Simmons & Uri Simonsohn
University of Pennsylvania

Word Count: 3,202

Forthcoming in Psychological Science
passages.label: Title, authors and publication status printed on the manuscript

passages.quote:
In their response to the failed replication, Carney, Cuddy, and Yap (2015) reviewed 33 successful
studies investigating the effects of expansive vs. contractive posing, focusing on differences between
these studies and the failed replication, to identify possible moderators that future studies could explore.
passages.label: Introduction: S4's description of S3 (Carney et al., 2015); S4's words, not S3's

passages.quote:
In this paper we rely on p-curve analysis to answer the following question: Does the literature
reviewed by Carney et al. (2015) suggest the existence of an effect once we account for selective
reporting? We conclude not.
passages.label: Introduction: question and stated conclusion

passages.quote:
We first evaluated if evidential value was present. As explained in Simonsohn et al. (2015), we
conclude that a literature contains evidential value if either the half p-curve (which only analyzes critical
p-values below .025) is significantly right-skewed at the 5% level, or if both the half and full p-curve are
significantly right skewed at the 10% level. Neither condition is met here (phalf=.11 and pfull=.63,
respectively).
passages.label: Results: test for evidential value
